name: 74HC595 Shift Register
summary: 8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register with a separate output latch. Three microcontroller pins buy you eight outputs, and chaining Q7S into the next chip's DS extends that indefinitely.
notes: Two clocks, and mixing them up is the classic bug: SH_CP (pin 11) shifts a bit into the register, ST_CP (pin 12) copies the whole register to the output pins. Shift all eight bits first, then latch once.
Data is sampled on the rising edge of SH_CP, so it is SPI mode 0 compatible, MOSI to DS, SCK to SH_CP, and any GPIO as the latch.
OE (pin 13) is active low and must be grounded for the outputs to drive. Tie it high to tri-state all eight outputs, or feed it PWM to dim an entire LED bank at once.
MR (pin 10) is active low and must be tied to VCC for normal operation. It clears the shift register but not the output latch.
Output current is around 6 mA per pin and 70 mA for the whole package. For LED matrices or relays use the TPIC6B595, which has 150 mA open-drain sinks.
Q0 is pin 15, on the far side from Q1-Q7. The output order on the package is not the order you would draw it.
HC inputs need a level near their own supply rail. A 5 V 74HC595 clocked from 3.3 V logic will drop bits, use the 74HCT595, which has TTL input thresholds, or run the register at 3.3 V.

pins.name: Q7S
pins.note: Wire to the next chip's DS to chain registers. This is the last stage of the shift register, not the latch, so it changes on SH_CP.

pins.name: MR
pins.note: Tie to VCC for normal use. Clears the shift register only, the latch keeps its value until ST_CP.

pins.name: SH_CP
pins.note: Rising edge shifts DS into the register. This is SCK.

pins.name: ST_CP
pins.note: Rising edge copies the shift register to Q0-Q7. This is the latch pin.

pins.name: OE
pins.note: Ground it to enable outputs. PWM here dims every output together.

pins.name: Q0
pins.note: First bit out, but physically opposite Q1-Q7.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: 100 nF decoupling at the pin; shift registers switch eight outputs at once.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit

parts.why: Eight outputs switching together is a real current step.
Active low output enable. Left floating the outputs stay tri-stated and nothing lights.
Active low clear. Left floating the register clears at random.

circuit.note: OE can take a PWM signal instead of a ground link, which dims every output at once.
